# Data dictionary — ground-truth validation workbooks

Generated by `scripts/04_analyses/build_groundtruth_sample.py`. **One row = one (paper,
reading stage).** A full-text paper has TWO adjacent rows — an `abstract` row and a
`full text` row (same reader). Abstract-only papers have one `abstract` row.

Dropdown values live on a hidden `Lists` sheet. Validation is **warning-style** — if the
right answer isn't offered, type it into the cell and keep it.

Column groups: paper info → Q1–Q11 → method ticks → 5 interaction blocks → wrap-up.

## Paper info (pre-filled, do not edit)
| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| `row_id` | stable id; `a`/`b` suffix = abstract/full-text row of a full-text paper (`K###` kappa, `B###` Bea, `I###` Ian, `M###` mock) |
| `paper_reviewed` | **you set this** — decides what else to fill: `complete` (fill the row) / `could not access the paper` / `review or secondary compilation` (Q1=no, Q3=review, Q4 only) / `not a fungus-in-plant study` (Q1=no, rest blank). Blank = not done yet. |
| `reading_stage` | `abstract` = read only the abstract in the sheet · `full text` = open doi_link, read the whole paper |
| `paper_id` · `doi_link` · `year` · `journal` · `title` · `abstract` | bibliographic + the abstract text |

On a `full text` row you may copy your `abstract` answers across, then correct / add what
the full text tells you. Both rows are kept. If `paper_reviewed = not applicable`, set
Q1 = `no` and leave everything else blank.

## Paper-level questions (the column header IS the question)
| Q | asks | notes |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | does this paper report a fungus coming from a plant? (yes/no/unclear) | false-positive gate |
| Q2 | paper's main purpose (single choice, 8 categories + other) | Referee 2 natural-products point; also the disciplinary-composition breakdown |
| Q3 | how were the fungi obtained in this paper? (single choice; "mixed methods (type which)"; "review — no new fungi") | flags NGS + review papers |
| Q4 | language of the text you are reading on this row | answer per reading_stage |
| Q5 | any sequence-only (uncultured) taxa? | OTU/ASV taxa — Referee 3 |
| Q6 | strain-level variation noted? (yes / no / only one strain) | Referee 2 strain point |
| Q7 | where was the plant SAMPLED? (free text; "not stated" — never the authors' institution) | |
| Q8 | what geographic info does the paper contain? (sampling stated / inferable / only affiliation / none) | Referee 2 geographic-attribution check |
| Q9 | biome — WWF terrestrial biome (Olson et al. 2001); list several if it spans them | |
| Q10 | how many distinct fungus-host pairs? (a number) | incl. any in the NGS summary |
| Q11 | was the surface-sterilisation checked? (yes-control / no / not a culture study / can't tell) | the classic endophyte QC — Referee 3 |

## Method ticks (the purple block) — `yes` for every method used (rubric)
`culture from sterilised tissue` · `microscopy in tissue` ·
`direct sequencing from tissue` · `isolate ID by sequencing` ·
`resynthesis / re-inoculation` · `method not stated`

## Interaction blocks 1–5 (each = one distinct fungus × host pair)
| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| `fungus_N` · `host_plant_N` | **verbatim as the authors name them** — record the authors' name even if the taxon has since been renamed (synonym resolution is programmatic, post hoc) |
| `tissue_N` | leaf / root / … — several tissues for one pair go in the one cell (`leaf, root`); "shoots" / "aerial parts" unsplit → `leaf, stem` |
| `fungal_lifestyle_N` | trophic mode — endophyte / plant pathogen / saprotroph / mycorrhizal / mycoparasite / … (FungalTraits primary_lifestyle, Põlme et al. 2020, condensed). *How the fungus lives.* |
| `effect_on_host_N` | net outcome for **this** plant — harmful / beneficial / neutral-commensal / no-symptoms-not-tested / not-reported. *What happened to the plant.* |
| `evidence_basis_N` | how the lifestyle + effect were established — tested here / observed here / inferred from the taxon / asserted / not stated |

`fungal_lifestyle` and `effect_on_host` are deliberately separate axes — a `plant
pathogen` lifestyle can occur with a `no visible symptoms` effect. That decoupling is the
study's central point.

## Wrap-up
`extra_pairs_or_NGS_community_summary` (pairs beyond block 5 + the OTU-table summary) ·
`anything_you_were_unsure_about`

(`date_reviewed` is on the **left**, 3rd column next to `paper_reviewed`, so review /
not-applicable rows need no horizontal scrolling. There is no `annotator_initials` column —
the workbook file name identifies the annotator.)

---

## How these become metrics (`score_groundtruth.py`, run later)
- **Interaction precision / recall / F1** — per paper and per reading stage, the pairs you
  listed vs the model's. Your list is the reference.
- **Field accuracy** — `tissue`, `fungal_lifestyle` (vs the model's guild), `effect_on_host`,
  `Q7 location`, `Q9 biome` on matched pairs / papers.
- **False-positive rate** — model interactions in papers you marked `Q1 = no`, plus
  model-only pairs. **False-negative rate** — pairs you listed the model missed.
- **Inter-annotator agreement** — Fleiss' κ across all raters on the kappa block, per
  field; disagreements adjudicated to consensus.
- **Abstract vs full text, human** — per full-text paper, the `abstract` row vs the
  `full text` row from the same reader → what abstracts omit. Feeds Task 1.
- **`fungal_lifestyle` × `effect_on_host`** — shows the same fungus with different host
  outcomes across studies ("location, not lifestyle"); commensalism etc. as its own
  category; and `evidence_basis` quantifies how often labels are `inferred` / `asserted`
  vs `tested` (the anti-circularity result).
- **`Q3` / method ticks / `Q5` / `Q11`** — the endophytism-QC breakdown Referee 3 asked for.
- **`Q8`** — the geographic-attribution breakdown Referee 2 c6 asked for.
